label: daemon cpu hot loop write path starvation root cause and fix evidence chunk 1
title: daemon cpu hot loop write path starvation root cause and fix evidence chunk 1
summary: The :8787 daemon pegging to 100-140% CPU and starving its WRITE path (POST /overlay/note 5-20s+, /state 30s timeouts while GETs served slowly) was NOT the drain lanes retrying, git snapshots, or the .git/GRAPH_CHECKPOINT touch error (that touch error is a benign worktree-commit hook artifact, harmless). A v8-inspector CPU profile (kill -USR1 <pid>, hand-rolled WS client to Profiler.start, 12k samples) traced the burn to buildGraph -> projectGraphFromNative, which loops every native task (~1268) and per task ran THREE whole-graph scans: judge.judgingState/unverifiedEdgesForNode scanned all overlay.edges (~5333) = O(tasks x edges) ~6.7M comparisons/build; depRefs did overlay.edges.filter(e=>e.to===key) per task (same class); harnessTranscriptForTask re-scanned all agents + re-Date.parse'd bounds per task. Each uncached build blocked the event loop for many seconds; any write bumps the overlay mtime, invalidating the snapshot cache so every /state/session/task re-ran the quadratic build -> write starvation. A SECOND layer: the headless drain (runDueDrains) re-loaded the overlay 3-5x PER TICK (findDueJudgeWork, backend-resolve, claimDueJudgeWork, review-merge gate + candidate scan), each running overlay.load -> graphStore.loadGraph = an 11MB checkpoint parse + read of ~2200 node JSONL files, continuously while idle. FIXES (minimal, behavior-preserving, all unit-tested): (1) judge.unverifiedIncidentSet(overlay) built once per build; judgingState(overlay,key,{unverifiedIncident}) does O(1) membership (legacy positional callers fall back to scan). (2) makeResolver builds an inbound-edge-by-target Map once; depRefs does O(1) lookup. (3) agentsBySessionIndex threaded as st.agentsBySession; authoritative when present (missing bucket => null, no O(agents) fallthrough). (4) an mtime-gated per-tick drain overlay cache (_drainOverlay, keyed on overlay-file+checkpoint+nodes-dir mtimes) threaded through every drain sub-call via the deps.overlay seam, collapsing 3-5 full graph parses per tick to one; a judge-claim save bumps the overlay mtime so a real change is never served stale. RESULTS: write latency 5-20s+ -> 0.1-0.3s (steady state); /state 30s-timeout -> ~0.5-2s warm; judgingState 29%->1%, harnessTranscriptForTask 34%->3%, depRefs 15%->gone in the profile; CPU no longer pinned (idle samples reach 0%, vs flat 100-140% before). DEPLOY NOTE for this env: ~/.claude/orchestrator is a SYMLINK to the repo checkout /Users/imyu/Desktop/zonoid, so the installed daemon IS the main working tree; the daemon's git ops are scoped to .graph only and never touch code files, so the fix must live in the working tree (or on main) for a restart to pick it up -- do NOT git-checkout-revert the code files after editing. Files: daemon.js, lib/judge.js, lib/headless-drain.js, test/judging-gate.test.js. REMAINING (not pathological): a one-time ~5-min-post-boot graph compaction pass and hasBlockingEdge/isReversePairedJudgeBlockingEdge per-build cost remain as bounded, non-starving work; a follow-up could index hasBlockingEdge similarly if further idle-CPU reduction is wanted.
